intro.title: Build typed state machine transitions
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, type-safe state machine that models a traffic light system. You will learn how to use TypeScript's union types and literal types to define a set of allowed states and transitions between them. The core concept involves creating a function that only permits valid state changes based on predefined rules. By the end, you will have a working typed state machine that prevents invalid transitions, helping you write more predictable and error-resistant code.
intro.usecase: Typed state machine transitions are essential in modern web applications where UI components have predictable states and behaviors. For example, form submissions follow clear states: idle, validating, submitting, success, or error—each with specific allowed transitions. E-commerce checkout flows use state machines to manage steps like cart review, shipping selection, payment processing, and order confirmation while preventing invalid transitions. In dashboards, data loading states (loading, loaded, error) and interactive filters rely on typed transitions to ensure UI consistency and prevent bugs. This pattern helps developers model complex workflows like multi-step wizards, authentication flows, or media players with type-safe guarantees.
